newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures end higher.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures end higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures retreated from their highs in afternoon trading but recovered late to settle mostly higher.

Traders said shortcovering that had dried up after the Treasury bond futures close reappeared to pull most indices near the top of the day's range. March Standard and Poor's 500 futures closed above key support at 804.00 to 804.50, a level that one analyst said was crucial for a firm tone on Monday.
Overall, traders said the market was relieved by the morning's U.S. jobs report, even though it showed a strong gain in February non-farm payrolls.
Traders said that overall, U.S. markets were a bit less spooked by the idea of an imminent credit tightening, even though expectations were intact for a rate hike down the road.

February non-farm payrolls rose 339,000, well-above 230,000 -- the average forecast of economists polled by Reuters. But traders said the focus turned to downward revisions in December and January jobs, and to a smaller than expected rise in hourly wages.
March S&Ps had shaved gains in earlier afternoon trade after a quiet close in Treasury bond futures and amid a sagging technology sector, but resilience soon returned.
February jobs rose 339,000, well above the average Reuters estimate of 230,000. But January's figure was downwardly revised and hourly wages were not as strong as many had thought, traders said.
"A 7000 print in the Dow -- that's a pretty good way to end the week," one S&P 500 futures trader said.
He called March S&Ps "pretty robust" and said more gains were on tap for early Monday. Traders pegged resistance at 812.50 to 812.70 and at 815.00.

March S&P 500s closed up 6.60 points to 807.20, NASDAQ 100s eased 11.00 to 845.00, Value Line futures were up 5.35 points at 720.10, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 210.0 to 18090.0 and Midcap 400s rose 0.95 points to 267.60.
